title: Enhance resume analyzer with comprehensive extraction and advanced features

requirements.text: Replace the mock AI parsing in aiResumeParser.ts with comprehensive extraction that captures contact information (phone, email, LinkedIn, location), professional summary, certifications with issuing organizations and dates, and languages with proficiency levels

quotes: More comprehensive data extraction (skills, education, certifications, contact information)

acceptanceCriteria: Contact information section displays phone, email, LinkedIn URL, and location when present in resume
Professional summary is extracted and displayed as a separate section
Certifications include issuing organization and date fields
Languages are extracted with proficiency levels (Basic, Intermediate, Fluent, Native)

requirements.text: Enhance work experience parsing to extract detailed information including job titles, company names, employment dates (start and end), location, and bullet-point descriptions of responsibilities and achievements for each position

quotes: Better work experience parsing with job titles, companies, dates, and descriptions
Detailed work experience parsing with job titles, companies, dates, and descriptions

acceptanceCriteria: Each work experience entry displays company name, job title, location, and date range
Employment dates are parsed into structured start and end date fields
Job descriptions are extracted as an array of bullet points
Work experience entries are displayed in reverse chronological order

requirements.text: Implement a resume scoring and analysis system that evaluates resumes based on completeness (presence of all sections), content quality (description detail, quantifiable achievements), formatting consistency, and skill relevance to common job requirements, displaying an overall score out of 100 with breakdown by category
acceptanceCriteria: Overall resume score is calculated and displayed as a percentage out of 100
Score breakdown shows individual category scores: Completeness, Content Quality, Formatting, and Skill Relevance
Each category includes specific feedback explaining the score
Scoring algorithm awards points for complete sections, detailed descriptions, quantifiable achievements, and in-demand skills

requirements.text: Redesign the results display page with a modern, professional UI featuring a card-based layout with clear visual hierarchy, section headers with icons, improved typography and spacing, color-coded skill tags, and responsive design that adapts gracefully to mobile devices
acceptanceCriteria: Results page uses a clean card-based layout with consistent spacing and shadows
Each major section (Contact, Summary, Experience, Education, Skills, Certifications) has a clear header with an appropriate icon
Skills are displayed as color-coded tags grouped by category
Layout is fully responsive and usable on mobile devices
Typography follows a clear hierarchy with appropriate font sizes and weights

requirements.text: Enhance the education section extraction to capture degree type, field of study, institution name, graduation date, GPA (if present), and relevant coursework or honors
acceptanceCriteria: Each education entry displays degree type and field of study
Institution name and graduation date are extracted and displayed
GPA is captured and displayed when present in the resume
Relevant coursework and honors are extracted as separate fields when available

requirements.text: Improve skills extraction to categorize skills into Technical Skills (programming languages, frameworks, tools), Soft Skills (communication, leadership, teamwork), and Domain Skills (industry-specific knowledge), with automatic proficiency level inference based on years of experience and context

quotes: More comprehensive data extraction (skills, education, certifications, contact information)

acceptanceCriteria: Skills are automatically categorized into Technical, Soft, and Domain categories
Proficiency levels (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced) are inferred from context and experience duration
Skills display includes visual indicators for proficiency level
Each skill category is displayed in a separate, clearly labeled section

constraints: Maintain the existing single-actor Motoko backend architecture
Do not modify immutable frontend paths: useInternetIdentity.ts, useInternetIdentity.tsx, useActor.ts, main.tsx, and components/ui directory
Keep the existing Resume data type structure in backend/main.mo and extend it rather than replacing it
Preserve the current authentication flow using Internet Identity
Maintain compatibility with existing resume upload and job role matching features
nonGoals: Integration with external resume parsing APIs or third-party services
Real-time collaboration features or multi-user editing
Integration with job boards or applicant tracking systems
Machine learning model training or custom NLP model implementation
Support for resume formats other than PDF
